title: Black-throated Trogon — ISO 12,800
subtitle: A black-throated trogon perched in rainforest in Costa Rica's Osa Peninsula, shot at ISO 12,800. Iridescent green plumage, a deep black throat, vivid yellow chest, and finely barred tail feathers give noise-reduction tools a demanding mix of saturated colour, fine detail, and graded tones to handle at very high ISO.

critique.text: This is the original RAW image, serving as the baseline, shot at a very demanding ISO 12800. Consequently, it exhibits severe luminance and chrominance noise across the entire frame, which significantly degrades sharpness, masks fine feather detail, and creates a highly distracting, grainy background. High-level overview: All other images in this set utilize various AI noise reduction tools to salvage this file, dramatically improving both noise levels and apparent sharpness by removing the heavy grain floor. My general ranking of how well the edits worked from best to worst is: DxO PureRAW (best), Lightroom AI, Topaz Photo, and finally ON1 (weakest of the edits).

Processed with DxO PureRAW 6. This image represents the most successful edit of the challenging RAW file. It expertly completely removes the heavy background noise, resulting in a buttery smooth bokeh. Crucially, it manages to extract the highest level of natural sharpness and micro-contrast from the bird's feathers and the mossy branch. Compared to the noisy RAW, the transformation is staggering, and it slightly edges out the Lightroom edit by providing just a hint more crispness without introducing any unnatural artifacts.

images.title: Lightroom Denoise
images.caption: Lightroom AI Denoise at default settings

critique.text: Processed with Lightroom AI Denoise. This is an excellent edit that strikes a superb balance. It completely eliminates the heavy ISO 12800 grain seen in the RAW file while maintaining a smooth, natural-looking background bokeh. The sharpness is vastly improved over the original, bringing out fine, realistic details in the bird's feathers and eye without the over-processed, plastic look seen in the Topaz version. It is highly effective and very close in quality to the DxO edit.

images.title: Topaz Photo
images.caption: Topaz Photos with default noise reduction running against raw image

critique.text: Processed with Topaz Photo at default settings. This image successfully removes the heavy noise present in the original RAW, but the noise reduction is arguably too aggressive. The out-of-focus background has taken on a slightly plastic, waxy appearance. While sharpness on the bird is significantly improved over the RAW, the feather details look somewhat painted or artificial compared to the Lightroom and DxO edits.

Processed with ON1 RAW NoNoise. While this edit improves upon the severe grain of the original RAW file, it struggles compared to the other AI tools. The noise reduction is inconsistent, leaving behind patchy, mottled color artifacts in the out-of-focus green background. The sharpness of the bird is improved compared to the RAW baseline, but the resulting texture feels a bit crunchy and less naturally resolved than in the Lightroom or DxO versions.
